question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Portuguese Naval Milestones and Locations]
options: Vasco da Gama's first arrival in India — Calicut (Kozhikode), 1498
Portuguese capture of Hormuz — Persian Gulf, 1515
Portuguese Estado da India headquarters — Cochin (Kochi)
wrong_fact: The headquarters of the Portuguese Estado da India was Goa (from 1510), NOT Cochin. Cochin was the earlier temporary base before Goa's capture.
explanation: Vasco da Gama arrived at Calicut on the Malabar Coast in 1498, opening the sea route to India. The Battle of Diu (1509) in the Arabian Sea was a decisive Portuguese victory over the combined Mamluk-Gujarati-Calicut fleet. Afonso de Albuquerque captured Hormuz at the mouth of the Persian Gulf in 1515, controlling the spice trade. However, the Estado da India (Portuguese Asian empire) was headquartered at Goa (captured 1510), not Cochin — though Cochin was briefly the first Portuguese base in India.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Portuguese Forts/Feitorias and their Locations]
options: Fortaleza de São Sebastião — Mozambique Island, East Africa
Fort of Malacca — Strait of Malacca, Malaysia
wrong_fact: Bassein Fort (Vasai Fort) was located on the Konkan coast north of Bombay (Mumbai), NOT on the Coromandel Coast near Madras.
explanation: Fort Manuel (later Fort Manueline) was the first European fort in India, built at Cochin in 1503. The Fortaleza de São Sebastião on Mozambique Island was a key Portuguese stronghold on the East African coast. The Portuguese captured and fortified Malacca in 1511, controlling the Strait of Malacca. However, Bassein (Vasai) Fort was on the Konkan coast (Maharashtra), north of Bombay — it guarded the Northern Konkan region, not the Coromandel Coast on India's southeastern side.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Portuguese Naval Admirals/Governors and their Key Actions]
options: Francisco de Almeida — First Viceroy of Portuguese India; won Battle of Diu (1509)
Afonso de Albuquerque — Captured Goa (1510), Malacca (1511), Hormuz (1515)
Vasco da Gama — Third Viceroy of Portuguese India; died at Cochin (1524)
Pedro Álvares Cabral — Discovered the sea route around Cape of Good Hope (1488)
wrong_fact: The sea route around the Cape of Good Hope was discovered by Bartolomeu Dias in 1488, NOT Pedro Álvares Cabral. Cabral led the second voyage to India (1500) and accidentally discovered Brazil.
explanation: Francisco de Almeida served as the first Viceroy of Portuguese India and won the decisive naval Battle of Diu (1509). Afonso de Albuquerque was the greatest Portuguese imperial strategist, capturing Goa, Malacca, and Hormuz. Vasco da Gama made three voyages to India; he died at Cochin as the third Viceroy in 1524. However, it was Bartolomeu Dias who first rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488 — Pedro Álvares Cabral commanded the second Portuguese fleet to India (1500) and accidentally landed in Brazil.
